guard: Ctrl-C on a foreground `cotal up` follows the same sparing rule as bare `cotal down` (#1307): the seat snapshot is taken while the manager still answers, the exact recorded manager's spare capability is asserted before any signal, the teardown is awaited before the broker is signalled, and the seats left behind are reported with the reap route. The handler is idempotent under a second Ctrl-C.
why: The suite drives the shipped foreground `up` as a real subprocess with a real managed seat (a shim
`claude` on PATH resolving to a real core-dist mesh endpoint), so a mutant that drops the spare
capability assertion or the spared report is observed through the teardown's real output and the
seat's real liveness, not inferred from a source string.
M1 (drop the spare-capability assertion) is the destructive regression this guard exists for: the
handler signals whatever the pidfile names without proving that exact manager can release custody.
An armed-intent mutant was tried first and is REFUSED by the shipped arm gate (it requires the
stop reservation only down's stopLocalProcess holds), which grades WRONG-RED: the design blocks
the armed shape, so the mutation that can actually reach operators is the missing assertion. With
it gone the snapshot drops with the same error path and the report cell is the first to notice.
M2 (remove the spared report) restores the pre-fix silence: the stack still tears down and the seat
still survives, but the operator is told nothing. Only the spared-report cell can notice, which is
why it is the named assertion.
Both mutations run the CLI as a subprocess, so they mutate a module only `dist/` delivers to it:
every mutation builds first and rebuilds in `afterRestore` (dist/ is gitignored; git cannot be the
recovery for a build compiled from the mutant).

mutations.name: M1 the handler stops asserting the spare capability, so an unverifiable manager is signalled blindly
mutations.expectRed: the spared report names the seat and the reap route
mutations.cell: the spared report names the seat and the reap route
mutations.note: The destructive regression this guard exists for: the handler skipping the exact-process spare assertion and signalling whatever the pidfile names. Without the assertion the capability file is never consulted, `spared` stays undefined (the snapshot is dropped with it on the same error path), and the operator is told nothing about live work while an unverifiable manager may have reaped it. The first cell that can notice is the spared-report cell. `void armManagerShutdownIntent` keeps the sibling import referenced so the healthy tree compiles identically with the assertion present or absent.

mutations.name: M2 the handler stops reporting the seats it left behind
mutations.expectRed: the spared report names the seat and the reap route
mutations.cell: the spared report names the seat and the reap route
mutations.note: The pre-fix silence: teardown still works and the seat still survives, but the operator is told nothing about live work while bare `down` reports it. Only the spared-report cell can notice, so it is the named assertion; the snapshot is still taken, so no earlier cell moves.
